sentences.text: The loan agreement describes the item as a penal charge of ₹500 per month of default, not as penal interest added to the rate of interest.

For this UCB, the applicable rule says penalty for non-compliance shall be treated as penal charges and shall not be levied in the form of penal interest added to the rate of interest charged on the advances.

On the evidence provided, I cannot say that the ₹500 monthly penal charge itself violates the prohibition on penal interest, because the record does not show it being levied as added interest rather than as a charge.

Missing: whether the charge is actually imposed as added interest in practice, and any sanction-date or other loan terms needed to test the remaining penal-charge conditions; I searched the agreement clause and the applicable UCB directions.
